claims.statement: `modules/attendance/` contains only a README that declares "No code yet" and lists `data/attendance.ts`, `domain/eligibility.ts` and `ui/` as planned; the trainer pages that would own the attendance workflow are self-contained placeholders that import no module.

The only live attendance read is an embedded `attendance_records(attendance_date, present)` select in the batch query, and `completedSessions()` counts distinct attended dates (a Set over `present` rows) while returning null when the batch has no snapshotted `total_sessions` or no attendance rows — because PostgREST answers an empty embed with `[]`, which would otherwise read as a real 0 sessions held.
`excused` and `notes` are absent from that embed, so nothing in the app can currently distinguish an excused absence from an unexcused one.

`mapBatchRow` sets `progressPct` from the stored, hand-typed `batches.progress_percent` column with an `orZero` default, while deriving `completedSessions` from attendance in the same object — so a single Batch holds a hand-typed percentage free to disagree with its attendance figure, contrary to ADR-001 B2's attendance-derived rule.

`sessionProgress()` returns null when either `completedSessions` or `totalSessions` is missing and caps its percentage at 100, and `describeSessionProgress()` renders that null as "Sessions not recorded"; `BatchCard` is the surface that honours it with an "Attendance not recorded yet" state.

`AnalyticsView` charts "Training progress by batch" from `b.progressPct` and its elapsed/remaining bars from the zero-defaulted `currentDay`/`totalDays` aliases, and `BatchTimeline` fills the training phase from `progressPct` while printing `Day currentDay/totalDays`; `batch.progressPct` stays non-nullable in `shared/types.ts` while `completedSessions`/`totalSessions` beside it are nullable, and the mapper marks the `currentDay`/`totalDays` aliases as compatibility shims that must not be rendered as a "Day X of Y" claim.

`metrics.ts` is the one aggregate that reads the attendance pair: its `sessionProgress` filters to batches with a non-null `completedSessions` and a `totalSessions`, and a test pins `sessionProgressPct: null` for a batch whose only signal is `progressPct: 90`.

ADR-007 Elig-2 supersedes ADR-001's `Elig` row: a scholar is dropped if total absences exceed 20% of the batch's `total_sessions` (allowed = floor of sessions × percent ÷ 100, so the next absence disqualifies) or on 3 consecutive unexcused absences, whichever trips first; the rule sits in `RULES.md`'s locked domain facts beside the progress formula. The retired rule was a fixed ≥5 absences, stored as `max_absences = 4`, and was a payment exclusion rather than an enrollment dropout.

The rule is unevaluable for two independent reasons a builder inherits: no per-learner attendance read exists (the embed is batch-level), and a batch with a null `total_sessions` has no denominator — the same condition that already makes `completedSessions()` return null.
`total_sessions` is a snapshot of nominal hours ÷ 8 taken at batch creation (E2/D3), so the denominator never moves with the calendar and is unavailable on a batch that never snapshotted one.

The "consecutive" half counts over consecutive *recorded* attendance rows ordered by `attendance_date` (Elig-4): no session-calendar table exists, so a date without a row is unmarked and must not be read as an absence — the ADR-004 "absent key ≠ evidence" caution applied to attendance.

Dropout is a computed signal, not an automated write (Elig-5): crossing a threshold surfaces an at-risk state while flipping `learners.is_active = false` stays a manual registrar action; `is_active` has existed on `learners` since the canonical migration and is read for nothing else yet.

FF2's final-tranche absence deduction (`tranche% × total_TSF − absences × ₱160`) is unchanged by ADR-007 and runs off the raw per-scholar absence count independently of the dropout threshold, so a scholar can accrue deductions for sessions attended before a dropout took effect (Elig-6).

The ADR-007 migration is additive and fully guarded (so a re-run is a no-op), and it lands the rule in three columns: `attendance_records.excused boolean not null default false` meaningful only where `present = false`, `program_billing_rules.max_absence_percent numeric(5,2) not null default 20.00` checked in (0,100], and a nullable, no-default `tenant_settings.max_absence_percent` whose null means inherit the program rule.
`excused` defaults to false as the compliance-safe direction — an absence nobody marked counts as unexcused, so forgetting to mark cannot excuse a scholar and understate dropout risk.

The threshold column is not a rename: `max_absences = 4` counted sessions while `max_absence_percent = 20.00` is a share of the batch's snapshotted `total_sessions`, so casting 4 to 4.00 would read as "4 percent" and allow one absence on a 45-session batch instead of nine; the old column is dropped from both tables rather than kept beside the new one.

The ADR-007 change had to ship as a new additive migration rather than an in-place edit of `20260910120000`: Supabase keys applied migrations on the version string, so editing a recorded file changes only the repository and the live column would have stayed `max_absences`; filename ordering makes the additive file correct whichever way the applied-state question lands, which RULES.md rule 20 makes the standing pattern for new migrations.

`attendance_records` rows stay editable in place with no lock flag even after billing (ADR-001 X2): INSERT and UPDATE policies admit `can_trainer_write_batch` or `can_manage_tenant`, while DELETE is `can_manage_tenant` only, so a trainer corrects by updating `present`/`excused` rather than deleting evidence — and the existing policy row already covers the new `excused` column, ADR-007 adding no policies.

The per-edit `activity_log` event X2 requires is convention, not a database trigger — no trigger writes it — so a new attendance write path must author its own event or the audit trail silently stops.

No code reads the ADR-007 columns: grep over `app/`, `modules/`, `shared/` and `lib/` finds neither `excused` nor `max_absence_percent`, `database.types.ts` carries neither, and `attendance_records` appears in code only as an inline embed shape — and ADR-007 records that no shipped code encoded the retired rule either, so this was a schema and docs correction rather than a refactor.

`modules/attendance/` contains only a README and no other file, so the planned `modules/attendance/domain/eligibility.ts` (and its `data/attendance.ts` sibling) must be written from scratch rather than extended from a partial eligibility layer.

`database.types.ts` may not be regenerated yet because it hand-carries `billing_deadline` ahead of its migration: until a database holds every object the file describes, ADR-007's application wiring must treat the two columns as possibly absent, and rule 20 requires regeneration before the mappers are updated.

`attendance_records` is unique on `(tenant_id, batch_id, learner_id, attendance_date)`, so a marking surface must resolve a second write for the same learner and date as an upsert or merge rather than a plain insert.

The existing test pins cover only the progress side — distinct-date counting and null `completedSessions` for an empty embed or null `total_sessions`, plus the null/cap behaviour of `sessionProgress()` — with nothing touching `excused`, `max_absence_percent` or a dropout boundary.

The two ADR-007 triggers are independent: the 3-consecutive-unexcused streak fires even while total absences remain under the percentage, so an evaluator must not short-circuit on "under threshold" and must report whichever trigger trips.

The percentage comparison is strict (`absences > floor(total_sessions × percent ÷ 100)`): exactly 20% of a batch's sessions is still eligible and the next absence disqualifies, so the threshold is not an inclusive cap.

`attendance_records.excused` affects only the consecutive-unexcused trigger: the percentage trigger counts absences whether excused or not, and `excused` is meaningful only on rows where `present = false`.

Threshold precedence is the program default with a per-tenant override (`tenant ?? program`, null in both falling back to the program default), but no shipped code resolves either column, so the precedence is documented rather than implemented and needs confirmation.

Billing readiness consumes the hand-typed `batch.progressPct` rather than attendance: `mapBatchRow` fills it from the stored `progress_percent` column with an `orZero` default, and `isBillingReady`/`billingGate` compare against that value, so the progress gate and the per-learner dropout signal read different sources.

`getBatchLearnersSnapshot` returns every learner regardless of `is_active` and leaves the exclusion policy to the caller, which is the hook an eligibility signal would use to hide dropped scholars from a roster rather than a fetch-time filter.

The attendance marking surface is a placeholder that only echoes `batchId` and states the later contract (verify the trainer is assigned before returning roster data or accepting writes), while the trainer dashboard is padding around a `MetricsRow` built from the batch snapshot with no attendance module import.

The attendance and batch-progress logic that exists sits in `modules/batches/*` rather than the owning attendance module, so a builder moving it must respect import direction (rule 7), `data/` privacy (rule 8) and the no-business-logic-in-`app/` rule (rule 11).
